axioms: A registry only eliminates fragmentation on the day every existing consumer resolves identity through it — a registry that some consumers still bypass via name-string joins is a fifth source of truth, not a single one.
Migrating a live registrant carries its accumulated history (trust scores, dispatch outcomes) as first-class state that must be explicitly re-attributed, not implicitly discarded by re-keying.

A registry's boundary (identity-only vs. identity-plus-lifecycle-plus-routing) determines how many systems a downstream consumer must still join across to make a decision — a narrow boundary can leave the net join-count unchanged even while claiming consolidation.
'Thin plugin' claims about blast radius must be evaluated against the number of consumers requiring read-path AND write-path changes, not just the size of the new plugin itself.

Rejecting a candidate home for a registry on architectural grounds (e.g., 'runtime substrate vs. plugin-layer concern') must hold up against how that candidate already touches the entities the registry would own, not just its stated charter.

Extraction precedent (thin single-responsibility plugins) only transfers cleanly when the new case has comparable consumer-cardinality to the precedent; a registry with N required consumers is a structurally different migration than a precedent with effectively one.
primitives: accumulated evidence carry-forward (trust rows, dispatch history)
single-source-of-truth convergence vs. relocation of fragmentation
failure_mode: Does not own how tracer evidence reaches an agent at review time or the freshness of that evidence — sees evidence-acquisition shape as out of scope, only cares that identity resolution is consistent regardless of what evidence backs a finding.
Blind to path-discovery/federation mechanics (hub doc resolution, nested-repo boundary walks) — treats 'where does the agent find companion-graph.json' as someone else's problem entirely.

Reasons in migration/consolidation terms and may underweight cases where staying fragmented is actually cheaper than a registry migration whose consumer-cardinality makes it expensive — can over-index on consolidation as inherently virtuous.
